The Ebonyi State Commissioner for Project Monitoring and Evaluation, Chief Sunday Inyima, has dismissed insinuations that the brutal murder of his younger brother, Mr. Egeonu Inyima, was politically motivated. He described such claims as misleading, false and fabricated in a statement on Tuesday in Abakaliki. Inyima maintained that his brother’s death had no political undertone, stressing that the deceased was not involved in any political dispute with anyone, contrary to insinuations in some quarters. He condemned those allegedly spreading unverified accounts of the incident, describing attempts to link the murder to political conflict as capable of creating unnecessary tension. He made the clarification while addressing members of the All Progressives Congress, Ohaukwu Local Government Area chapter, who visited his country home in Izhiangbo to commiserate with him over the incident. Add us to your Preferred Sources The deceased was allegedly killed by some suspected assailants at Umuogudu-Oshia Ngbo in the Ohaukwu Local Government Area of Ebonyi State. 2027: Yahaya Bello, Natasha battle for Kogi Central votes PDP, APGA, Accord backing Tinubu’s reelection bid – APC chair NDC vows fresh primaries as Bauchi gov candidate quits The commissioner described the killing as unfortunate, barbaric and regrettable. He assured the public that the family, in collaboration with security agencies in the state, would do everything within their power to unravel the circumstances surrounding his brother’s death. He equally urged relevant law enforcement agencies to ensure that justice was served without distortion, warning individuals and groups against interfering in ways that could jeopardise the investigation and legal process. “Though I am severely traumatised by the gruesome murder of my younger brother, I would not want anyone to suffer unjustly. No innocent person should be implicated or made to suffer for a crime he or she did not commit. “I appeal to the police and other relevant authorities handling the matter to be transparent, conduct a thorough investigation and bring the perpetrators to justice. “Nobody, and I mean nobody, regardless of their status, including myself, should interfere in the matter. The legal process must be allowed to run its course until justice is fully served,” he said. Edward Nnachi
